017package org.apache.juneau.examples.mcp;
018
019import java.net.*;
020
021import org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.*;
022import org.apache.juneau.microservice.*;
023import org.apache.juneau.microservice.jetty.*;
024import org.eclipse.jetty.ee11.servlet.*;
025import org.eclipse.jetty.server.*;
026
027import jakarta.servlet.*;
028
029/**
030 * Boots {@link ExampleMcpServer} on an embedded Jetty server.
031 *
032 * <p>
033 * Run {@link #main(String[]) main} to start the server on a fixed port (default {@code 5000}, or pass a
034 * port as the first argument) and leave it running so you can point {@link ExampleClient} (or any MCP
035 * client) at it. The in-process end-to-end test uses {@link #start(int) start(0)} to boot on an
036 * OS-assigned ephemeral port instead.
037 *
038 * <p>
039 * The wiring mirrors Juneau's own test fixture: a Jetty {@link Server} plus the {@link ExampleMcpServer}
040 * servlet are placed in a {@link BasicBeanStore}, and {@link JettyConfiguration} (added via
041 * {@link org.apache.juneau.microservice.Microservice.Builder#configurations(Class...)}) auto-mounts the {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.Rest @Rest}
042 * servlet at {@code "/"} and drives the server lifecycle. Because the {@code Server} is supplied as a bean,
043 * we control the listen port directly &mdash; no {@code jetty.xml} required.
044 */
045@SuppressWarnings({
046   "java:S106" // Example walkthrough intentionally prints to stdout; console output is the demo's deliverable.
047})
048public final class ExampleServer implements AutoCloseable {
049
050   /** Default listen port used by {@link #main(String[])} when none is supplied. */
051   public static final int DEFAULT_PORT = 5000;
052
053   private final Microservice microservice;
054   private final URI rootUrl;
055
056   private ExampleServer(Microservice microservice, URI rootUrl) {
057      this.microservice = microservice;
058      this.rootUrl = rootUrl;
059   }
060
061   /**
062    * Starts the example MCP server.
063    *
064    * @param port The TCP port to listen on, or {@code 0} to let the OS assign an ephemeral port.
065    * @return A running server handle. Close it (or call {@link #close()}) to stop.
066    * @throws Exception If the server fails to start.
067    */
068   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // The bean store is handed to (and closed by) the Microservice lifecycle.
069   public static ExampleServer start(int port) throws Exception {
070      var jetty = buildServer(port);
071
072      var beanStore = new BasicBeanStore();
073      beanStore.addBean(Server.class, jetty);
074      beanStore.addBean(Servlet.class, new ExampleMcpServer());
075
076      var microservice = Microservice.create()
077         .beanStore(beanStore)
078         .configurations(JettyConfiguration.class)
079         // This example has no interactive commands to offer; skip the Java console entirely so
080         // startup doesn't print "Could not create console command" for whatever default console
081         // commands a discovered config might otherwise register.
082         .consoleEnabled(false)
083         .build();
084      microservice.start();
085
086      return new ExampleServer(microservice, URI.create("http://localhost:" + boundPort(jetty) + "/"));
087   }
088
089   /**
090    * Returns the root URL the server is listening on (e.g. {@code http://localhost:5000/}).
091    *
092    * @return The root URL. Never <jk>null</jk>.
093    */
094   public URI getRootUrl() {
095      return rootUrl;
096   }
097
098   @Override
099   public void close() throws Exception {
100      microservice.stop();
101   }
102
103   /**
104    * Runs the server until the process is killed.
105    *
106    * @param args Optional single argument: the port to listen on (defaults to {@link #DEFAULT_PORT}).
107    * @throws Exception If the server fails to start.
108    */
109   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // example server runs for the JVM lifetime; closed on process exit.
110   public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
111      var port = args.length > 0 ? Integer.parseInt(args[0]) : DEFAULT_PORT;
112      var server = start(port);
113      System.out.println("Juneau MCP example server is listening at " + server.getRootUrl());
114      System.out.println("Drive it with:  ExampleClient " + server.getRootUrl());
115      System.out.println("Press Ctrl-C to stop.");
116      // Microservice.join() defaults to a documented no-op, so it won't actually block here; join the
117      // main thread directly to keep the process (and the Jetty daemon threads it started) alive.
118      Thread.currentThread().join();
119   }
120
121   /** Builds a Jetty server with a single connector on {@code port} and a root servlet context. */
122   @SuppressWarnings("resource") // connector is added to and owned by the server; closed when the server stops.
123   private static Server buildServer(int port) {
124      var server = new Server();
125      var connector = new ServerConnector(server);
126      connector.setPort(port);
127      server.addConnector(connector);
128      var handler = new ServletContextHandler();
129      handler.setContextPath("/");
130      // JettyServerComponent discovers the handler via this attribute (same convention as jetty.xml).
131      server.setAttribute("ServletContextHandler", handler);
132      server.setHandler(handler);
133      return server;
134   }
135
136   /** Reads the actual bound port (meaningful even when the server was started on port 0). */
137   private static int boundPort(Server server) {
138      for (var connector : server.getConnectors())
139         if (connector instanceof ServerConnector sc)
140            return sc.getLocalPort();
141      throw new IllegalStateException("Could not determine the bound port of the Jetty server.");
142   }
143}
